explanation.text:
The Psalmist celebrates the blessedness of those who compassionate the poor, conduct strongly contrasted with the spite of his enemies and neglect of his friends in his calamity. He prays for God's mercy in view of his ill desert, and, in confidence of relief, and that God will vindicate his cause, he closes with a doxology. (Psa 41:1-13)

God rewards kindness to the poor (Pro 19:17). From Psa 41:2, Psa 41:11 it may be inferred that the Psalmist describes his own conduct.

poor--in person, position, and possessions.

bsb.title: For the choirmaster. A Psalm of David.
bsb.text: Blessed is the one who cares for the poor; the LORD will deliver him in the day of trouble.

explanation.text:
shall be blessed--literally, "led aright," or "safely," prospered (Psa 23:3).

upon the earth--or land of promise (Psa 25:13; Psa 27:3-9, etc.).

bsb.text: The LORD will protect and preserve him; He will bless him in the land and refuse to give him over to the will of his foes.

explanation.text: The figures of Psa 41:3 are drawn from the acts of a kind nurse.

bsb.text: The LORD will sustain him on his bed of illness and restore him from his bed of sickness.

explanation.text:
I said--I asked the mercy I show.

heal my soul--(Compare Psa 30:2). "Sin and suffering are united," is one of the great teachings of the Psalms.

bsb.text: I said, “O LORD, be gracious to me; heal me, for I have sinned against You.”

explanation.text: A graphic picture of the conduct of a malignant enemy.

bsb.text: My enemies say with malice: “When will he die and be forgotten?”

explanation.text:
to see me--as if to spy out my case.

he speaketh . . . itself--or, "he speaketh vanity as to his heart"--that is, does not speak candidly, "he gathereth iniquity to him," collects elements for mischief, and then divulges the gains of his hypocrisy.

bsb.text: My visitor speaks falsehood; he gathers slander in his heart; he goes out and spreads it abroad.

explanation.text: So of others, all act alike.

bsb.text: All who hate me whisper against me; they imagine the worst for me:

explanation.text:
An evil disease--literally, "a word of Belial," some slander.

cleaveth--literally, "poured on him."

that he lieth--who has now laid down, "he is utterly undone and our victory is sure."

bsb.text: “A vile disease has been poured into him; he will never get up from where he lies!”

explanation.text:
mine . . . friend--literally, "the man of my peace."

eat . . . bread--who depended on me or was well treated by me.

hath lifted up heel--in scornful violence. As David and his fortunes typified Christ and His (compare Introduction), so these words expressed the treatment he received, and also that of his Son and Lord; hence, though not distinctly prophetical, our Saviour (Joh 13:18) applies them to Judas, "that the Scripture may be fulfilled." This last phrase has a wide use in the New Testament, and is not restricted to denote special prophecies.

bsb.text: Even my close friend whom I trusted, the one who shared my bread, has lifted up his heel against me.

explanation.text: A lawful punishment of criminals is not revenge, nor inconsistent with their final good (compare Psa 40:14-15).

bsb.text: But You, O LORD, be gracious to me and raise me up, that I may repay them.

explanation.text: favourest--or tenderly lovest me (Gen 34:19), evinced by relief from his enemies, and, farther, God recognizes his innocence by upholding him.

bsb.text: By this I know that You delight in me, for my enemy does not triumph over me.

explanation.text: settest . . . before thy face--under thy watch and care, as God before man's face (Psa 16:8) is an object of trust and love.

bsb.text: In my integrity You uphold me and set me in Your presence forever.

explanation.text:
Blessed--praised, usually applied to God. The word usually applied to men denotes happiness (Psa 1:1; Psa 32:1). With this doxology the first book closes.

Next: Psalms Chapter 42

bsb.text: Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, from everlasting to everlasting. Amen and Amen.
